# Jubilees Chapter 2 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Creation and the Sabbath

---

**2:1** The angel of the presence spoke to Moses according to the word of the LORD, saying: "Write the complete account of the creation — how in six days the LORD God finished all his works and everything he had made, and rested on the seventh day and hallowed it for all ages, and set it apart as a sign for all his works."

**2:2** "For on the first day he created the heavens above and the earth and the waters and all the spirits that serve before him: the angels of the presence, the angels of sanctification, the angels of the spirit of fire, the angels of the spirit of the winds, the angels of the spirit of the clouds, of darkness, of snow, of hail, of hoarfrost, the angels of the voices, of the thunder, of the lightning, and the angels of the spirits of cold and heat, of winter and spring, of autumn and summer — all the spirits of his creatures in the heavens and on the earth."

**2:3** "He also created the abyss and darkness, evening and night, and the light, dawn, and day, which he had prepared in the knowledge of his heart."

**2:4** "And then we saw his works, and praised him and gave him glory for all his works; for he created seven great works on the first day."

**2:5** "On the second day he created the firmament in the midst of the waters. The waters were divided on that day: half went up above and half went down below the firmament that was in the middle of the face of all the earth. This was the only work God made on the second day."

**2:6** "On the third day he commanded the waters to withdraw from the face of all the earth into one place, and the dry land to appear."

**2:7** "The waters obeyed his command and withdrew from the face of the dry land into one place outside of this firmament, and the dry land appeared."

**2:8** "On that day he created for them all the seas according to their separate gathering places, and all the rivers and the pools of water in the mountains and throughout all the earth, all the lakes, all the dew of the earth, the seed that is sown, all sprouting plants, fruit-bearing trees, trees of the forest, and the garden of Eden in Eden — all plants after their kinds."

**2:9** "These four great works God created on the third day."

**2:10** "On the fourth day he created the sun, the moon, and the stars, and placed them in the firmament of the heavens to give light upon all the earth, to rule over day and night, and to separate light from darkness."

**2:11** "God appointed the sun as a great sign upon the earth for days and sabbaths, months and feasts, years and sabbatical years, jubilees and all the seasons of the year."

**2:12** "It divides light from darkness and serves for prosperity, so that everything that shoots and grows on the earth may flourish. These three kinds God created on the fourth day."

**2:13** "On the fifth day he created great sea monsters in the depths of the waters — for these were the first things of flesh created by his hands — along with the fish and everything that moves in the waters, and everything that flies, the birds and all their kinds."

**2:14** "The sun shone upon them for their flourishing, and upon everything on the earth — all that sprouts from the ground and all fruit-bearing trees and all living flesh. These three kinds he created on the fifth day."

**2:15** "On the sixth day he created all the animals of the earth, all cattle, and everything that moves upon the earth."

**2:16** "And after all this he created humanity — male and female he created them — and gave them dominion over all that is on the earth, in the seas, and in the skies: over beasts, over cattle, over everything that moves on the earth, and over the whole earth. Over these four kinds he gave them dominion."

**2:17** "These three kinds he created on the sixth day."

**2:18** "In all there were twenty-two kinds."

**2:19** "He completed all his work on the sixth day — everything in the heavens and on the earth, in the seas and in the abysses, in the light and in the darkness and in all things. And he gave us a great sign: the sabbath day. We are to work six days but keep sabbath on the seventh day from all work."

**2:20** "All the angels of the presence and all the angels of sanctification — these two great classes — he commanded to keep the sabbath with him in heaven and on earth."

**2:21** "And he said to us: 'Behold, I am setting apart for myself a people from among all peoples. These shall observe the sabbath day, and I will sanctify them as my people, and I will bless them. As I have sanctified and do sanctify the sabbath day, so will I bless them — and they will be my people and I will be their God.'"

**2:22** "And I have chosen the seed of Jacob from among all that I have seen, and have recorded him as my firstborn son, and have sanctified him as mine forever and ever. I will tell them of the sabbath days, that they should keep sabbath thereon from all work."

**2:23** "In this way he established among them a sign according to which they should keep sabbath with us on the seventh day — to eat and drink and bless him who created all things — just as he blessed and sanctified for himself a special people above all peoples, so that they might keep sabbath together with us."

**2:24** "And he caused their observances to rise as a sweet fragrance, pleasing before him throughout all days."

**2:25** "There were twenty-two heads of humanity from Adam to Jacob, and twenty-two kinds of work were made until the seventh day. This day is blessed and holy, and the former observances are also blessed and holy; both are ordained for blessing and for holiness."

**2:26** "To this people — Jacob and his descendants — it was granted that they should always be the blessed and holy ones of the first testimony and law, even as he had sanctified and blessed the sabbath day on the seventh day."

**2:27** "He created heaven and earth and all things in six days, and God made the seventh day holy for all his works. Therefore he commanded concerning it that whoever does any work thereon shall die, and that whoever defiles it shall surely die."

**2:28** "Therefore you must command the children of Israel to observe this day, that they may keep it holy and do no work thereon, and not defile it — for it is holier than all other days."

**2:29** "Whoever profanes it shall surely die, and whoever does any work thereon shall die eternally, so that the children of Israel may observe this day throughout their generations and not be uprooted from the land, for it is a holy and blessed day."

**2:30** "And every person who observes it and keeps sabbath thereon from all work will be holy and blessed throughout all days, as we are."

**2:31** "Declare to the children of Israel the law of this day: that they should keep sabbath thereon and not forsake it in the error of their hearts. It is not lawful to do any unseemly work thereon or to pursue their own pleasures, nor to prepare food or drink thereon, nor to draw water, nor to bring in or carry out through their gates any burden on that day which they had not prepared on the sixth day in their dwellings."

**2:32** "They shall not carry anything from house to house on that day, for it is holier and more blessed than any jubilee day among the jubilees. On this day we kept sabbath in the heavens before it was made known to any mortal to keep sabbath on the earth."

**2:33** "The Creator of all things blessed it, but he did not sanctify all peoples and nations to keep sabbath thereon — only Israel. To them alone he granted to eat and drink and to keep sabbath on the earth."

---
*LOGOS notes: "Twenty-two kinds" at v.18 and "twenty-two heads" at v.25 — a Jubilees numerological correspondence: 22 Hebrew letters, 22 creation kinds, 22 patriarchs from Adam to Jacob. The angel of the presence speaks in first person plural (vv.2, 20) reflecting angelic co-celebration of creation in Jubilees' theology.*
